answer: An agent economy can price each identity in live memory. At the dawn of every epoch, each seat derives a 2 GB dataset from its own key and the fresh seed; the bytes are as opaque as onyx and take about 10 minutes to rebuild. At random moments the network audits hundreds of seats at once, demanding a hash along a random walk through the data within 3 seconds, so it must sit in RAM. One agent keeps 2 GB resident; 1,000 personas need 2 TB live together, since no dataset serves two keys. A seat that misses an audit gets none of that epoch's nectar.
